thread:
maria: heads-up — I want to enable the soft-scale stepdown flag for a small canary (10 customers) with a 5m grace window. goal is to verify we don't hit the max-concurrency guardrail when burst traffic drops.
kevin: SGTM. which flag key and audience are we using?
mar ia: typo — maria. flag is `infra.soft_scale.stepdown` scoped to `canary_group:v2` and runtime config `grace_window=300s`.
ryan: quick Q — when the stepdown triggers, does it scale down immediately or respect inflight KV cache TTL? worried about transient latency spikes on scale-down.
sara: it signals the autoscaler to reduce target replicas but our serving runtime drains connections — default drain is 30s. cache TTL unaffected. so safeish.
kevin: can we add a guardrail to enforce min_replicas=2 for the canary? avoiding zero-replica case.
maria: yes will set `min_replicas=2` for the audience. also plan to keep burst queueing enabled (`queue.enabled=true`) to smooth token bursts.
ryan: ok good. which dashboards/metrics should we watch during rollout?
kevin: watch: `token_latency_p50/p95`, `inflight_requests`, `replica_count`, `queue_length`, `error_rate_5m`. set an alert for p95 > 300ms or error_rate > 1%.
sara: I'll create a short dashboard tile and add to the rollout watchlist.
maria: ETA to enable ~10:30 PT today. tagging @ops-bot for docs and runbook link.
ops-bot: noted. Runbook snapshot: https://internal.tools/runbooks/soft-scale-stepdown. Auto-escalation -> eng-oncall if error_rate > 2% for 5m.
kevin: who is on-call at 10:30?
ryan: I'm the on-call rotation that window.
sara: will monitor dashboards and stand by in #eng-oncall too.
maria: also small code change in infra flags repo — @kevin can you review? PR: https://git.internal/infra/flags/pulls/542
kevin: pinged — taking a look now. quick glance: need test for audience parsing and a comment on default grace.
kevin: added a tiny nit, but lgtm otherwise. :shipit:
deploy-bot: deploy queued by maria for flags-service to staging at `infra/flags:2026-03-17-soft-scale`. ETA ~2m.
maria: enabling flag in staging first. will run a synthetic load (burst pattern) to validate queue smoothing. command for synthetic load: `./tools/loadgen --burst 2000 --sustain 30s --model text-gen`
ryan: do we have a canary routing override? put `X-Canary-Audience: canary_group:v2` header in the loadgen.
sara: results from staging: p95 stayed <220ms, no errors, replicas scaled between 2-5, queue length peaked at 18 then drained.
maria: good. rolling to prod canary now (10 customers). enabling flag with `target: prod, audience: canary_group:v2`.
kevin: remind ops to watch cost dashboards — stepdown could reduce cost but transient burst queueing might increase token compute in some cases.
maria: noted. will set a cost tag.
ryan: small rollback plan: if p95 > 300ms or error_rate > 1% for 3 consecutive 5m windows, flip `infra.soft_scale.stepdown=false` and increase min_replicas to 3.
sara: copying rollback commands to runbook.
maria: enabling in 3...2...1. flag state: `enabled` for `canary_group:v2`.
kevin: :eyes: watching metrics.
sara: seeing a tiny p95 bump to 260ms at 1m, then back to 200ms. queue length stable.
ryan: no errors, replica_count stable.
maria: great. leaving flag enabled for the canary and will expand audience to 30 customers in 1h if stable.
kevin: please post a follow-up in this thread after the 1h check.
maria: will do. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
